answer: Beacon reputation stops Sybils in four steps. First, a newcomer registers under a beacon that timestamps its first job, so no identity can backdate history. Second, it completes five paid trial jobs, each receipt signed by a real client and pinned to the beacon. Third, peers audit one random trial weekly, and a failed audit freezes the account ninety days. Fourth, after twenty clean trials the bond unlocks. Faking 1,000 agents needs 5,000 trials plus 1,000 bonds, over $150,000 lost if caught. Trust grows slow like timber around a lagoon: only work that survives seasons earns the light.
